ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in the Cartesian coordinate system $xOy$, the line $l_1$ passes through points $A(0, 1)$ and $B(2, 2)$. The line $l_1$ is translated downward by $m$ units to obtain the line $l_2$, which is known to pass through point $(-1, -2)$ and intersects the x-axis at point C. What is the equation of the line $l_1$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Let the equation of line $l_1$ be $y=kx+b$,\\
since line $l_1$ passes through points A(0, 1) and B(2, 2),\\
thus $\begin{cases}b=1\\ 2k+b=2\end{cases}$, solving yields: $\begin{cases}k=\frac{1}{2}\\ b=1\end{cases}$,\\
therefore, the equation of line $l_1$ is $y= \frac{1}{2}x+1=\boxed{\frac{1}{2}x+1}$.
